slides.title:
1,000 shoppers
stormed a store
for an *"ugly" doll*.
slides.sub: Retail price: $21. Here's how it happened 👇

slides.title:
Georgia art student Xavier Roberts
starts hand-making *soft
sculpture dolls*.
slides.sub:
He learned an old German fabric technique
in college. First name: "Little People"
(FOX Television Stations).

slides.title:
You didn't buy one.
You *adopted* one, with an
official-looking paper.
slides.sub:
Each doll was "born" in a cabbage patch.
Roberts even built "BabyLand General
Hospital" in Georgia (ABC7, FOX).

slides.title:
Toy giant Coleco signs on
and starts *mass-producing*
the Cabbage Patch Kids.
slides.sub:
Coleco told Time it expected to sell
2.5 million dolls in the 1983 season
(FOX; WJLA).

slides.title:
people storm a Zayre store in
Wilkes-Barre, PA. *The manager
grabs a baseball bat.*
slides.sub:
Late November 1983. One woman breaks
a bone, four others are hurt 
(NYT via WJLA; Time via FOX; ABC7).

slides.title:
shoppers rush a store in
Charleston, W.Va., that has
*only 120 dolls*.
slides.sub:
"It got ugly," the manager told Time.
(Time via FOX Television Stations; WJLA.)

slides.title:
dolls adopted in 1983.
$21 in stores, *resold
for $50 to $75*.
slides.sub:
20 million by 1985 (WJLA).
National Toy Hall of Fame in 2023
(FOX; WJLA).

slides.title: There's never been a toy like this. *I wish we had 10,000 to sell.*
slides.author:
Ronald Ladowski
Assistant manager, Zayre, Milwaukee
(The New York Times, 1983, via WJLA)

slides.title:
Sell the story,
*not just the product*.
slides.sub:
A $21 doll nobody called pretty won
Christmas because it came with a story.
Black Friday is Nov. 27. Be ready.
